help.title: Getting started
help.subtitle: Turn a photo into a low-poly triangulation in three steps.

load.title: 1. Load an image
load.body: Use the image button at the bottom of the modifier bar, the vertical strip of tools to the right of the canvas. Its icon is a picture with an arrow pointing up. Pick any photo to polygonize.

points.title: 2. Generate the base points
points.body: Open Point generation in the right panel. Drag Min radius all the way down to its minimum, then use Max radius to control density. Start around the middle or a little below, then refine. A smaller max packs in more, finer triangles.

emphasize.title: 3. Emphasize what matters
emphasize.body: Decide which shapes you want to keep crisp. Pick a tool from the modifier bar (polyline, curve, or circle) and draw over that feature. For example, trace a line along an edge. Press Space to apply, Esc to cancel.

help.footer: Save your work as a project anytime, or export the result as SVG, PDF, or an image from the top bar.

cursor.label: Cursor
cursor.tip: Hover the canvas to highlight the nearest modifier, click to select. Esc or ~ returns here.

polyline.label: Polyline
polyline.tip: Click to add vertices. Space or click the first vertex to finish, Esc to cancel.

catmullrom.label: Catmull-Rom curve
catmullrom.tip: Click to add control points. Space or click the first to finish, Esc to cancel.

circle.label: Circle (center & radius)
circle.tip: Click a point on the edge, then the center.

circle3.label: Circle (3 points)
circle3.tip: Click three points on the circle to fit it.

modifiers.title: Modifiers
modifiers.hint: Non-destructive layers over the base points. Pick a tool on the left; select a card to edit its points on the stage. Drag cards to reorder or to move them between groups.

newGroup.label: New group
newGroup.tip: Create a group to organize modifiers.

modifiers.dragCard: Drag the card to reorder or move into a group

pointGen.title: Point generation
pointGen.hint: Bridson Poisson disk with variable radius from Sobel edges. Edges get min radius (dense); flat areas get max radius (sparse). Changes reseed the base (modifiers are kept).

color.title: Color
color.hint: Color sampled from the image. Changes recompute all colors.
